newsitem.title: USA: AT&T posts expected decline in operating income.
newsitem.headline: AT&T posts expected decline in operating income.

text.p: AT&T Corp. reported an expected decline in third quarter operating earnings Wednesday while most regional Bell companies posted robust gains.
AT&T, which had announced last month that it expected its earnings to fall short of year-ago results and Wall Street's expectations, said its income from continuing operations fell 11 percent.
Meanwhile, local phone companies BellSouth Corp., Bell Atlantic Corp., SBC Communications Inc. and Pacific Telesis all reported stronger earnings.

AT&T reported net income of $1.43 billion, or 89 cents a share, up from $262 million, or 16 cents a share, in the year-ago period when it took a one-time charge of $1.6 billion for its restructuring and for cost reductions at its NCR computer unit.

The company had projected last month that its income from continuing operations would be lower in the third quarter. Operating earnings fell to $1.36 billion, or 84 cents a share, from $1.53 billion, or 96 cents a share.
AT&T said on Sept. 24 that its income from continuing operations might fall as much as 10 cents short of Wall Street analysts' expectations of income equal to 92 cents a share.
It said its operating income was hurt by competitive pressure in the long-distance telephone market, customer care enhancements and investments in local, on-line and wireless capabilities.
The telecommunications giant's revenues in the latest quarter were $13.2 billion, up from $12.9 billion.
AT&T's stock was down 12.5 cents at $39.75 in late afternoon trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
BellSouth Corp., which provides local telephone services in the Southeast, reported record operating income and sales for the quarter.
Net income was up 12.9 percent at $631 million and revenues were up 9 percent at $4.83 billion.
Atlanta-based BellSouth also said it added a record number of new telephone lines.
"This is the highest profit from operations for any quarter in the company's history," said Chairman John Clendenin.
BellSouth added a total of 222,000 telephone lines in its southern service area during the quarter, a record rate for the third quarter, the company said.
Philadelphia-based Bell Atlantic Corp., which provides local telephone service in the mid-Atlantic states, said its profit was up 9.4 percent and its sales were up 7.6 percent.

Bell Atlantic said it earned $483 million, or $1.10 a share, which compared with income of $441.9 million, or $1.01 a share. The year-ago results excluded a one-time gain of about $203 million from the sale of cellular properties and charges of about $40 million associated with some business development ventures and contracts.
Revenues rose to $3.30 billion from $3.26 billion.
SBC Communications Inc., the San Antonio, Texas-based parent of local telephone company Southwestern Bell, said it earned a record $593 million on record sales of $3.6 billion in the third quarter.
SBC said revenue of its telephone operations increased 8.5 percent. Over the last 12 months, residential access lines increased 3.7 percent and business lines grew 8.4 percent.

The company said it earned $593 million, or 97 cents a share, on revenue of $3.60 billion, which compared with a year-ago loss of $2.82 billion, or $3.75 a share, on revenue of $3.29 billion. The year-ago loss came after an extraordinary $2.8 billion charge for change in accounting standards.
Pacific Telesis, which provides local telephone service in California and Nevada, said it earned $286 million, or 67 cents a share, on revenue of $2.42 billion.

A year earlier, San Francisco-based PacTel lost $3.09 billion, or $7.22 a share, on sales of $2.28 billion. The year-earlier period included a one-time charge of $3.36 billion, or $7.86 a share, for a change in accounting procedures.
